title: Egg
text: “No, well… something about someone kicking up a fuss about wanting to sleep next to me.”
“Honestly… what’s with this bizarre back-and-forth all the way out here in the mountains, Naofumi? Or, wait, was that you, Motoyasu?”
“The one at fault here is the one stealing Father’s precious sleep time!”
I pointed at Rival’s parent.
“You lot are just kicking up a ridiculous fuss over nothing, that’s all.”
“You insolent dragon! In the first place, it’s your fault for suggesting we meet up later.”
You’re the one who cut into Father’s sleep time, after all.
“Yeah, yeah. Wasting time arguing over whose fault it is isn’t going to help anyone. If you want to go home and sleep, let’s just wrap up business quickly, all right?”
“Fine, that’ll do.”
“The rest of you, if you want to head back soon too, try not to cause a scene.”
With that warning from Father, we all fell quiet and settled in to watch how things would play out.

So it turned out Rival’s parent had brought along part of the treasure he’d gathered, meant for Father to use as child-rearing and living expenses for Assistant. Sold off, it would no doubt fetch a decent sum. Unfortunately, outside of Melromarc I’d already been securing plenty of treasure myself by hunting dragons and griffins, so money was hardly something I was short on. What we were apparently here to do was help carry this treasure that had been brought over as child support, indeed. We’d received something in a similar situation before, come to think of it.
“And then…”
What Rival’s parent brought out next was… what looked to be the egg from which Rival would be born. I recognized it right away, having seen it before.
…Something was wrong. By this point in time, it should’ve hatched already without question—so why hadn’t it? Even I couldn’t just stand by and watch quietly on this one.
“Pardon me. Why hasn’t that egg hatched yet?”

I kept as much distance as I could while pointing my spear at the egg that was supposed to hatch into Rival. To begin with, this was a situation where it wouldn’t have been the least bit strange for a non-looping Rival to have already popped its head out as if it were the most natural thing in the world. Just what was going on here?
“Motoyasu-kun, do you know something?”
“I do indeed. This is something that ought to have hatched by now without a doubt.”
“What are you two talking about?”
“Ah, right—Motoyasu-kun here is a Spear Hero who carries knowledge of the future, and it seems he’s had all sorts of encounters with Wyndia-chan.”
“Hoh… I found it hard to believe at first, given how much this one reeked of Filolial… but he healed me with magic and then beat me black and blue right after, didn’t he.”
Rival’s parent glared at me. What of it? Would he rather I’d finished him off on the spot? Not that it frightened me in the least, I say.
“So… about that egg Motoyasu-kun’s so worried about—is there something going on with it?”
“Hmm… well, I suppose it’s fine, since I was planning to make use of it regardless. This egg here… is meant to hatch into someone who’ll become a little sister to Wyndia.”
“An egg meant to become a little sister, huh.”
“Indeed. I thought it might be good for Wyndia’s upbringing. I’d entrusted her with the care of my new child, but… for some reason, it simply stopped hatching.”
Rival’s parent said this while lightly resting a hand on the egg.

“The egg refusing to hatch no matter how long we waited struck me as odd too, so I looked into it various ways… and it turns out some strange magic has been worked into it. I’ve been scratching my head over just when such a thing could have been done.”
“So going by what Motoyasu-kun’s saying, it should’ve hatched by now but hasn’t…”

It suddenly occurred to me—Rival had once thrown the egg it had been born from away into another world. Apparently, whenever Rival looped, it rigged something into the spear through some method or other. There was a good chance that, at the same time, it was also remotely tampering with its own original egg somehow. From what I heard from Rival later, before its egg hatched, it apparently triggered a soul-summoning spell through the spear. It mentioned something about transferring the memories recorded inside the spear onto that soul. Also, out of Rival’s own stubborn insistence that it alone would be Assistant’s little sister, it had rigged things so no new soul could ever enter the egg. According to Rival, having itself split into multiple copies across different loops would just be awkward, so it had set this up in advance. Whenever I looped, it would check its own life status through the Dragon Vein—if dead, it would possess the nearest dragon egg; if alive… it had all sorts of contingencies arranged like that. Though of course, none of this was something I knew at the time.
“So, since it wasn’t going to hatch anyway, I’d left it stored safely in my den, but it occurred to me it would make for an extremely convenient tool, so I brought it along to put it to use.”
“It’s not going to hatch, right?”

“Right, and that’s exactly why it makes such an excellent vessel for me to possess. Fortunately, the magic for it seems doable. Wyndia’s seemed quite hurt lately too, so if this could cheer her up even a little, I’d be glad…”
When it came down to it, Rival’s parent was the one who still hadn’t managed to graduate from doting on Assistant.
“A father possessing his daughter’s body to pretend to be her little sister…”

If ever there were a textbook definition of a pervert, this was it. Then again, this was something Rival’s parent did all the time. And the whole affair always ended with him getting sealed away into a compact as the final step, as a matter of course.
“It can’t be helped, since Wyndia’s the one who says she wants a little sister! Don’t overthink it!”

Hoh… so Rival’s gender had been Assistant’s choice all along. Come to think of it, Doctor had once told Father that a dragon’s gender could be chosen before hatching, and as a result, Rival’s adoptive little brother back in the original world had ended up male. That one’s chocolate had ended up causing quite the incident, as I recalled. Part of the reason the current Rafumi even existed traced back to him. During that whole fiasco, he’d split off from the chocolate monster at the last possible moment to save Father. Self-inflicted as it was, the story went that right after handing over the chocolate Father had rejected and returned—since it seemed a shame to waste it—to the chocolate monster that wanted it, the thing went berserk and swallowed him whole, and that was the root cause of it all.
“Hey.”
“…What?”
Ren was the one calling out to Rival’s parent.
“Dragons and Filolials don’t get along, right? Can you drive off the Filolials that keep coming after me?”
“It’s just the Filolials taking it upon themselves to hate us dragons. Those things… they had their fun tormenting me.”
It seemed he was still holding a grudge over having been beaten senseless by Yuki-chan and the others.
“As for whether I could drive them off… well, if you lot were to help me grow stronger, it might just be possible.”
“I see. Then I’ll lend a hand too. Power-leveling’s not exactly my thing, but… let’s say, in exchange for helping Wyndia settle in properly, you’ll cooperate with me. Now get to it!”
“Ren, just what are you plotting, I wonder?”
At my question, Ren furrowed his brow.
“Isn’t it obvious? Kuro’s fine since he’s off playing with Rafumi, but this is a plan to deal with Luna somehow. I’ll need to get Keel in on it too.”
“I won’t allow it! In that case, I’ll power Luna-chan up to the absolute limit!”
“That’s my own business.”
“Ren… you really can’t handle Kuro-chan and Luna-chan that much, huh.”
A cheap trick like that wasn’t going to work on me.
“I don’t quite follow, but I can’t overlook dragging Wyndia into something so bizarre.”
“If she ends up staying under Naofumi’s roof, she’ll understand it whether she likes it or not, and get dragged in regardless.”
“Whether she’ll actually understand is anyone’s guess, isn’t it.”
“True enough. We’re the ones left out of the loop.”
“Vof.”
Rabbit Guy and the others voiced their honest reaction to Ren’s remark.
“Come to think of it, Luna-chan, who loves cute things, once declared that Rabbit Guy’s demi-human form was on the cuter side, didn’t she?”

I remembered this well, having been targeted myself once while in usaunny form. It was only thanks to Keel and Ren being around that Luna-chan’s cravings for cute things stayed in check—without them, there was no doubt it would spread like wildfire to someone else. After all, without them around, she’d even taken to doting on Mole to an extreme degree. Chasing after Ren turned into an inult form, doting on him endlessly—now that was a nostalgic memory. In the previous loop, I’d occasionally turn Ren into an inult while he slept. In retaliation, he once blew my house sky-high with a skill.
